page: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processors clocked at 3.525 GHz, providing 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 256.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage includes 2577 GB of integrated local SSD capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The configuration does not include discrete GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements reveal high multi-core compute and throughput capabilities. Multi-threaded evaluations highlight strong performance across the PassMark CPU score (62169.0), stress-ng multi-core (86362.29), and Geekbench multi-core (17931.0). The instance excels at parallel workloads, demonstrated by high Clang software compilation (40132.0), ray tracing (61795.0), and PassMark encryption tests (68645.59). Memory subsystem results are led by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3045.5 and cached read bandwidth reaching 4155.63 GB/sec, although large uncached read and write bandwidth remain in the middle tier at 118.48 GB/sec and 66.51 GB/sec, respectively.

In transactional and data processing tests, the D64ads_v5 records strong execution rates, including 63.62 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a strong PassMark database operations rating of 26506.5. For CPU-based language model inference, it sustains strong token generation across small and medium models (328.91 tokens/sec on 135M and 27.98 tokens/sec on 7B architectures), though prompt processing for 70B models drops to an average 12.67 tokens/sec.

The qualitative cost-efficiency profile of the D64ads_v5 is driven by its dense CPU core count and included 2577 GB local SSD storage, which reduces the need for auxiliary attached disks for scratch space and caching. The instance lacks specialized vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 or AMX, limiting dense matrix and specialized AI workloads. It is best suited for large enterprise relational databases, distributed caching layers, software compilation clusters, and multi-threaded analytical processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v5 is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores with multithreading) running on a 3.525 GHz AMD EPYC 7763 processor, 256.0 GB of memory, and 2577 GB of bundled local SSD storage. It delivers strong multi-core performance across tests like Geekbench multi-core (17931.0) and PassMark CPU (62169.0), backed by top-tier PassMark memory results (3045.5). In-memory database workloads demonstrate high throughput, achieving 63.62 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database scores. Lacking discrete GPUs and AVX-512 extensions, the instance trades advanced matrix acceleration for dense, general-purpose multi-threaded capacity and high-speed temporary storage. It is primarily suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caches, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and enterprise application servers.
